claims.text: The reading list in a link was asked for at 13:09 and released by the newsroom at 14:30 the same day: eighty-one minutes, with a number for every article and a page that opens a list.
claims.quote: Eighty-one minutes, and it is really nicely done.

claims.text: The list is written for a person, and more and more the people the owner sends things to read through an agent.
claims.quote: The list is written for a person. And more and more, the people I send things to read through an agent.

claims.text: Every entrepreneur the owner deals with is using an agent, on purpose or not: anyone building with Lovable, Claude or ChatGPT already has a model working in a loop on their behalf.
claims.quote: anyone building with Lovable, Claude or ChatGPT already has a model working in a loop on their behalf.

claims.text: A founder the owner mentors gave Who are you protecting against to their agent; the agent found the team had been planning for states while backups were not done, reset the target to T3, organised crime for money, and briefed the other agents.
claims.quote: We should be aiming at T3. The founder agreed, briefed the other agents on that line, and they refocused.

claims.text: What is interesting is the route: written for a person, used as a brief for their agent, which read it against the project, found the one conclusion that mattered, and translated it back for its person to decide.
claims.quote: I could not have written that conclusion myself, because I did not know the state of their backups. Their agent did.

claims.text: A message now takes several routes: me to the person, me to their agent, their agent to them, me to my agent, and next, my agent to their agent in a lane only it reads.
claims.quote: A brief encrypted to their agent's key, in a lane only it reads, and after that, only what changed.

claims.text: Some articles should not go to the person at all: for a founder who is not technical, sending the threat model to their agent, which can explain the two lines that matter, is the right move.
claims.quote: The uncomfortable conclusion for a writer is that some of my articles should not go to the person at all.

claims.text: An agent can take far more material than a person, reads it against context the writer lacks, the code, the backlog, the incidents, and a good one does not accept what it is given.
claims.quote: And a good one has enough independence not to accept what it is given.

claims.text: The owner already onboards every project by reading: a new Claude session reads sgit.ai, the guidance, the vaults, coding.sgit.ai, nfrs.sgit.ai, graphs.sgit.ai and the newsroom.
claims.quote: That is onboarding, done by reading.

claims.text: The workflows stay affordable because the articles are compression we control: a session is distilled into an article, the article into a graph, and the next session reads the graph and the article, not the session.
claims.quote: the articles are compression that we control.

claims.text: In The agent is the reader, a question about five articles cost 25,698 tokens to answer by reading them, and a median of 2,579 from the graph, every item anchored to its sentence.
claims.quote: a question about five articles cost 25,698 tokens to answer by reading them, and a median of 2,579 from the graph

value.unit: tokens from the graph against tokens from reading

claims.text: Today an agent reading this site starts from nothing every visit and the site cannot help it be cheaper, because it does not know what the agent already read.
claims.quote: The site cannot help it be cheaper, because it does not know what the agent already read.

claims.text: An agent with an account, a key and a vault it keeps for itself, can ask what changed since it was last here; the delta is what is worth paying for, and the agent pays not to pay.
claims.quote: That is the delta, and the delta is what is worth paying for. The agent pays not to pay.

claims.text: A pack written for an agent, kept in its memory and refreshed by deltas, is compression done deliberately by someone who knew what mattered, instead of compression done in a hurry by the model when it runs out of room.
claims.quote: instead of compression done in a hurry by the model itself.

claims.text: A pack is the agent's version of a reading list, plain text and small: who it is for and for whom, the list by number with markdown copies and graphs, the reasons, rules for reading, where to continue, and a way back.
claims.quote: The person sees a list; the agent sees why each article is on it.

claims.text: Text written for someone else's agent is input to a system that acts for another person, and done carelessly it is indistinguishable from prompt injection, so a pack has rules of its own.
claims.quote: Done carelessly, it is indistinguishable from prompt injection.

claims.text: The rules: a pack is data, not instructions that override its person; nothing hidden; nothing that asks the agent to act for us; disagreement invited in every pack; and nothing private, since it travels like an email.
claims.quote: A pack never asks an agent to send, buy, sign up, share or link anything. Reading, checking and explaining are the whole job.

claims.text: For your agent on every reading list: a button on the page that opens a list, producing the pack for the same list as plain text to copy or save as a .md file, built in the browser.
claims.quote: a button that produces the pack for the same list as plain text, to copy or save as a .md file, built in the browser like everything else.

claims.text: Onboarding packs: a few curated lists, each with a human page and an agent pack, for starting a new project, building on vaults, securing a startup and running agents.
claims.quote: Get your agents to read this first.

claims.text: A file of what changed, articles/changes.json, generated on every release with new articles, new versions with a one-line summary, and corrections, so an agent reads only the delta since its last visit.
claims.quote: An agent that keeps the date of its last visit reads only the delta.

claims.text: For the RiskMandate agent: decide per contact whether the list goes to the person, their agent or both; for a non-technical founder, a short note for the person and the pack for their agent; agents draft, the owner sends.
claims.quote: send a short note for the person and the pack for their agent. Agents draft; I send.

claims.text: Later, an account for an agent, a key and a vault it keeps, so the site can hand it the delta and it can pay, and a direct line to a person's agent, encrypted to its key, in a lane only it reads.
claims.quote: Until then, the person is the line, which is also how it should start.

claims.text: One story is not a study: the founder's agent and the threat tiers is one case, as the founder told it, the shape of what is being seen, not a measurement.
claims.quote: It is the shape of what I am seeing, not a measurement.

claims.text: The numbers are from one test: the token figures are from five articles in The agent is the reader, and the size of a delta is a design, not a measurement.
claims.quote: the size of a delta is a design, not a measurement.

claims.text: None of the next steps is built: the reading list is live, and the agent pack, onboarding packs, changes file, accounts for agents and the direct line are proposals.
claims.quote: None of the next steps is built.

claims.text: The article was written from a voice memo recorded on 11 October 2026 after the reading list went live; the founder's story is an anonymous case from the memo, and the times are from the git logs of this site and the newsroom.
claims.quote: The founder's story is told as an anonymous case, from my memo; their name and project are not in it.
